result.topic_en: Worked example of a lunar eclipse computation: the Sun's apparent diameter, parallax and hourly motion, the Moon's apparent diameter, parallax and hourly motions, the semidiameter of the Earth's shadow, and the eclipse parameters a, b, A, B derived from them.
result.transcription:
378 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA.

§ 2. Ut igitur ex observatione quoque has res eruamus, primo diametrum solis apparentem [?] ejus parallaxin quaeramus, ex ejus anomalia excentrica
$V = 11^s 28^\circ 25' 22''$, unde fit $\sin V = -\sin 1^\circ 34' 38''$ et $\cos V = +\cos 1^\circ 34' 38''$.
Erat ergo diameter solis apparens $= 1933'' - 32'',2 = 1901'' = 31'41''$, ejus ergo semidiameter [?] apparens $= 15' 50\tfrac{1}{2}''$. Porro autem ejus parallaxis horizontalis erit $= 12''$. Tum vero motus horarius [?] solis erit $= 143'' = 2'23''$.

§ 3. Pro luna vero, cum sit ejus anomalia excentrica
$\varphi = 4^s 26^\circ 26' 6''$, $\sin\varphi = +\sin 33^\circ 33' 54''$, $\cos\varphi = -\cos 33^\circ 33' 54''$,
reperietur secundum praecepta supra data
diameter lunae apparens . . . . . $= 33' 15''$
semidiameter apparens . . . . . . $= 16\ 37\tfrac{1}{2}$
parallaxis lunae horizontalis . . . . $= 60\ 18$
Tum vero quoque invenietur
motus lunae horarius verus . . . . $= 37\ 20$
motus autem horarius nodi erit . . $= 0\ 8$.
Jam ad semidiametrum umbrae inveniendum, secundum regulam cognitam
ad parallaxin lunae horizontalem . $= 60\ 18$
addatur parallaxis solis . . . . . . $= 12$
summa $= 60\ 30$
subtrahatur semidiameter solis . . $= 15\ 50\tfrac{1}{2}$
eritque semidiameter umbrae . . . $= 44\ 39\tfrac{1}{2}$

§ 4. Ut igitur formulas supra Cap.... inventas ad hunc casum accomodemus, erit
semidiameter umbrae . . . . . . . . . $\alpha = 44' 39\tfrac{1}{2}'' = 2679'',5$
semidiameter lunae apparens . . . . . $\beta = 16\ 37\tfrac{1}{2} = 997,5$
ergo pro initio ac fine eclipsis . . . . $\alpha + \beta = 3677'' = f$
et pro immersione et emersione . . . . $\alpha - \beta = 1682 = F$
tempus ab initio eclipsis ad finem . . $h = 3^h 19' 45'' = 3^h, 32916$
tempus ab immersione ad emersionem $H = 1\ 3\ 25 = 1, 05694$
motus horarius solis . . . . . . . . . $m = 143$
motus horarius lunae . . . . . . . . . $n = 2240$
motus horarius nodi . . . . . . . . . . $k = 8$
ergo erit $m + k = 151$, $n + k = 2248$, $m + n + 2k = 2399$ et $n - m = 2097$; unde invenitur [?]
$lh = 0,5223355$, $la = 3,5731018$, $lA = 3,0748184$
$lH = 0,0240521$, $lb = 2,4002825$, $lB = 1,9019991$
ergo $a = 3742''$, $b = 251''$, $A = 1188''$ et $B = 80''$. Cum jam porro sit
longitudo umbrae . . . . . . . . . . . $= 9^s 6^\circ 51' 7''$
et longitudo nodi vera tabularis . . . . $= 3\ 2\ 34\ 24$

items.quote: Ut igitur ex observatione quoque has res eruamus, primo diametrum solis apparentem [?] ejus parallaxin quaeramus
items.english: So that we may also derive these things from observation, let us first seek the apparent diameter of the Sun [and] its parallax.

items.quote: Jam ad semidiametrum umbrae inveniendum, secundum regulam cognitam
items.english: Now, to find the semidiameter of the shadow, according to the known rule.

items.quote: Ut igitur formulas supra Cap.... inventas ad hunc casum accomodemus
items.english: In order to apply the formulas found above in Chapter ... to this case.
